title: CoCA: Criterion-Aware Credit Assignment for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.17733v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) evaluates responses against explicit criteria to construct rewards, offering a viable way to train large language models on open-ended tasks. However, standard methods compress criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards and assign uniform token advantages, leaving structured rubric supervision underutilized. Recent work seeks finer-grained guidance by treating rubrics as privileged information to derive self-distillation targets, but the resulting learning signal is not grounded in criterion outcomes and can lead to reward degradation. This motivates us to reframe the problem as criterion-aware credit assignment, where privileged rubric information serves as a relevance cue for credit allocation rather than a source of imitation targets. translated_title: CoCA：面向基于量规的强化学习的准则感知信用分配
translated_abstract: 基于量规的强化学习（RL）通过对照明确的标准来评估响应以构建奖励，为在开放式任务上训练大型语言模型提供了一种可行的途径。然而，标准方法将准则级别的反馈压缩为标量奖励，并分配统一的token优势，导致结构化的量规监督未被充分利用。最近的工作试图通过将量规视为特权信息来推导自蒸馏目标，从而获得更细粒度的指导，但由此产生的学习信号并未基于准则的实际结果，可能导致奖励退化。这促使我们将该问题重新构建为准则感知的信用分配，其中特权量规信息作为信用分配的相关性线索，而非模仿目标的来源。据此，我们提出了CoCA，它从组相对结果中推导准则级别的信用，并根据准则诱导的信号将这些信用分配到各个token上。
tldr: 提出CoCA方法，将量规信息作为相关性线索而非模仿目标，从组相对结果中推导准则级别的信用并分配到token上，从而更充分地利用基于量规的强化学习中的结构化监督。
en_tdlr: CoCA reframes rubric-based RL as criterion-aware credit assignment, using rubrics as relevance cues rather than imitation targets to derive criterion-level credits from group-relative outcomes and allocate them across tokens, thereby better exploiting structured rubric supervision.
